Parse a local Bank of Japan response snapshot

Source: R/snapshot.R
read_boj_snapshot.Rd

Parses one saved Bank of Japan (BOJ) response body with the same normalization used by the network-facing readers. This function is fully offline: it never opens a network connection, writes to the readboj cache, or changes the source file. The package's small inst/extdata examples are deterministic synthetic fixtures, not official BOJ observations.

Usage

read_boj_snapshot(
  path,
  type = c("data_json", "data_csv", "metadata_csv"),
  db,
  language = "en",
  encoding = "UTF-8",
  max_bytes = 128 * 1024^2,
  max_rows = 50000L
)

Arguments

path

Character path to an existing regular local response-body file. The returned provenance records its normalized path and exact SHA-256.

type

Response kind: "data_json", "data_csv", or "metadata_csv". The default expression selects "data_json".

db

BOJ database identifier used to populate the normalized db column; it is normalized to uppercase after validation.

language

For type = "data_csv", response language "en" or "jp"; Japanese CSV is decoded as CP932. It is still validated for other types but does not alter their parsing.

encoding

Character encoding passed to the metadata CSV reader when type = "metadata_csv"; use "UTF-8" or "CP932" for the supported BOJ encodings.

max_bytes

Positive maximum input bytes checked before parsing. The default is 128 MiB; oversized snapshots raise readboj_size_error.

max_rows

Positive whole-number maximum rows for data_csv and metadata_csv. The default is 50,000; it is ignored for data_json.

Value

A base data.frame with stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row names reset, and a readboj_provenance attribute containing source = "local response snapshot", the normalized path, raw_sha256, semantic_sha256, byte count, parser schema and package version. For type = "data_json" or "data_csv", the exact columns, in order, are character db, series_code, name_en, name_jp, unit_en, unit_jp, frequency, category_en, category_jp; Date last_update; character period; Date date; numeric value; and character raw_value and value_status. date is inferred from the frequency/period pair and may be NA; JSON nulls use value_status = "null", while CSV blank values use value_status = "blank". For type = "metadata_csv", the exact columns, in order, are character db, series_code, name_jp, name_en, unit_jp, unit_en, frequency, category_jp, category_en; integer layer1–layer5; character start_time and end_time; Date last_update; character notes_jp and notes_en; and logical is_series. The metadata parser always retains both language columns. semantic_sha256 excludes the volatile JSON DATE field for JSON input, canonicalizes the decoded CSV DATE line for observation CSV input, and is NA for metadata CSV input; raw_sha256 always covers the exact file bytes.

Details

type = "data_json" parses an API JSON response, type = "data_csv" parses an observation CSV, and type = "metadata_csv" parses a five-row preamble followed by a metadata CSV. The default type selects "data_json". language is validated for every call and selects CP932 for Japanese observation CSVs; it is otherwise ignored for JSON and metadata snapshots. encoding is used for metadata CSV decoding; "UTF-8" and "CP932" cover the package fixtures and official routes.

The file size is checked against max_bytes before parsing. For CSV inputs, max_rows is an inclusive materialisation bound; it is not used for JSON responses because JSON observations are already bounded by the response body and parser structure. For data_json and data_csv, non-success API statuses, malformed schemas and duplicate db/series_code/period identities fail closed rather than silently dropping or collapsing rows. A metadata_csv input is expected to contain the five-row BOJ preamble and is parsed as a tabular metadata file; its preamble is skipped without interpreting an API status field. Missing JSON values remain rows with an explicit status marker, and CSV blank markers remain observable in raw_value.

Errors and side effects

Missing paths, directories, invalid database/language values, oversized inputs, known observation-status/schema/identity failures, and metadata row limits are checked by the package and use typed readboj_*_error conditions where applicable. Unsupported type values and some low-level malformed or encoding/bound inputs may instead retain base-R or dependency errors and warnings. The function only reads path; it does not perform network I/O, create cache directories, or write files.

Examples

json_path <- system.file("extdata", "api-data-page-1.json", package = "readboj")
json_data <- read_boj_snapshot(json_path, type = "data_json", db = "FM08")
json_data[c("series_code", "period", "value", "value_status")]
#>   series_code period  value value_status
#> 1    SYNTHM01 202601 101.25     observed
#> 2    SYNTHM01 202602     NA         null
#> 3    SYNTHM01 202603 103.75     observed

csv_path <- system.file("extdata", "api-data-en-page-1.csv", package = "readboj")
csv_data <- read_boj_snapshot(csv_path, type = "data_csv", db = "FM08")
csv_data[c("series_code", "period", "value", "value_status")]
#>   series_code period  value value_status
#> 1    SYNTHM01 202601 101.25     observed
#> 2    SYNTHM01 202602     NA        blank
#> 3    SYNTHM01 202603 103.75     observed

metadata_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "metadata-bilingual-utf8.csv", package = "readboj"
)
metadata <- read_boj_snapshot(
  metadata_path, type = "metadata_csv", db = "FM08", encoding = "UTF-8"
)
metadata[c("series_code", "name_en", "name_jp", "is_series")]
#>   series_code                 name_en      name_jp is_series
#> 1                   Synthetic heading     合成階層     FALSE
#> 2    SYNTHM01 Synthetic monthly index 合成月次指数      TRUE
#> 3    SYNTHM02  Synthetic monthly rate 合成月次金利      TRUE
